frames.cueText: Same transported prefix shown as direct and Anger images, then assignment disagreement; benchmark stays reference only.
Click Stop: the acquisition stops and keeps its data; the counts no longer change, the inputs stay locked and the button reads Continue.
Click Continue again: the same acquisition continues and its counts keep growing; stop it again with Stop.
Click Reset acquisition again and confirm with Discard: the data are discarded, the status reads Ready and the inputs unlock; the button reads Start again.
Click Continue; after completion choose Compare. Both paths show the same retained prefix, with direct ideal deposit energy beside the acquired Anger path.
Click Reset acquisition and confirm with Discard. Compare returns to its start state.
Open Export report…. Choose HTML, PDF, Word or Event data. Cancel closes the format popup without writing.
Private dialog step — picture suppressed · Native dialog closed; export outcome visible in Studio
Open Export report…, choose Word and click Export…. In the save dialog enter a destination, check the filename and Save. Keep the same-name scene sidecar.

Choose Baseline in Preset: the fields now hold the 12 × 12 pixel, rank-7 reference geometry, still read-only.
Choose Detector: its Face view draws the detector face for these settings, captioned Settings for the next acquisition.
Type 3 in Pixels / side. The geometry is refused — the tab reads Detector pixels must be an integer from 4 to 64. — and Start does not start: the status bar gives the reason.
Hold the pointer over a cell of the flood map: the line under the image reads x 6.3 mm, y -4.5 mm · 10 counts — the cell's centre in millimetres (x to the right, y up, 0 on the axis) and its counts.
Choose the distance tool (accessible name Distance tool) above the measurement table and drag across the flood map: the table gains a row with the length in millimetres.

Choose the ROI tool (ROI tool (region of interest)) and drag a rectangle on the flood map: the table gains the sum over the whole pixels whose centres lie inside, and the line under the table gives its size and pixel count.
Click the icon button whose tooltip reads Clear all measurements: the table is emptied.
Select the Optics tab: the engineering geometry replaces the source list in the left panel.

Choose Waveform, then its view tab Four outputs (A–D). With the default direct crystal assignment there are no four outputs: the view reads Available with the experimental physical readout and offers Choose readout….
Choose Detector, then its view tab SiPM: the physical readout views are empty in the same way.
Press Ctrl+1 through Ctrl+5 to select Imaging, Spectrum, Waveform, Detector and Compare respectively.
Click the icon button whose tooltip reads Remove selected source: the selected source is removed.
Click Continue and wait until the acquisition completes. While acquired data exist the source fields and the add and remove buttons are locked, so the images always belong to the scene shown.
Confirm with Discard: the acquisition is discarded and the source fields unlock for the next acquisition.
Click Continue and wait until the acquisition completes.
Choose Spectrum: the histogram of measured energies with a band at each emission line, and the line table with the counts inside each band.
Type 2 in N × FWHM at each line and leave the field: each band widens to twice the FWHM at its line and the table recounts; the histogram itself does not change.
Tick Log Y again: the counts axis becomes logarithmic, so small and large bins can be read together; the data are unchanged.
